en-US.description:
Learn to copy Morse code (CW) by ear, the way real operators do.

Another Morse Trainer teaches you with the proven Koch method: it starts with two characters and adds the next one only when you're ready, building real instant recognition instead of counting dots and dashes.

MANY WAYS TO TRAIN

Learn the characters
• Journey: a leveled path from letters through punctuation, prosigns, Q-codes, abbreviations and words to call signs, with an unlock map and saved progress.
• Characters: the Koch-method ladder through A-Z and 0-9.
• Confusion Drill: targeted reps on the exact pairs you keep mixing up.

Copy real content
• Common Words: copy whole ham-radio words at speed, or bring your own list.
• Abbreviations and Q-Codes: the CW shorthand you'll hear on the air.
• Prosigns: run-together signals like AR and SK.
• Short Stories: 32 bundled fables, longer classics with a bookmark, or today's real news headlines, hidden until you decode them.

Build speed
• Head Copy: hold a whole word in your head, then grade your own recall.
• Type It: free recall with no multiple choice to lean on.
• QRQ Speed: high-speed copy at 35, 40, 50 or 60 WPM.
• Rapid Fire: call signs, words, number groups or states sent back to back.
• Daily Dit: one five-letter word a day, the same for everyone. Guess it from the code; every replay or miss slows the code down until you catch it.

Play
• Six arcade games that train by ear: Morse Invaders, CW Galaga, Morse Defender, CW Dungeon, CW Frogger and CW Asteroids. Every hit and miss feeds your stats.

Get on the air
• Pileup Runner: call CQ and pull callsigns out of a simulated pileup, with QSB, QRN, cut numbers, busted calls and a live log.
• Contest: timed runs of five real weekly CW events (K1USN SST, ICWC MST, CWops CWT, NCCC Sprint, ARRL Field Day) with a live score and scorecard.
• Code Exam: the classic FCC/ARRL-style copy test at 5, 13 or 20 WPM.
• Repeater: live CW with real operators over the Vail network.

Send, decode and look up
• Sending Practice: key it back on a touch key or a hardware MIDI key, with live decode of what you actually sent.
• Sending Drills: printable practice sheets built from what you've studied.
• CW Decoder: point the microphone at a rig or a WebSDR and read received Morse as text.
• Reference: a tap-to-hear chart of prosigns, Q-codes, abbreviations, ham lingo and cut numbers.
• Listen & Learn: hands-free, eyes-free practice: hear the code, then the answer spoken aloud. Keeps playing with the screen locked.

BUILT FOR REAL PRACTICE
• Character speed up to 60 WPM, Farnsworth spacing and sidetone pitch.
• Answer by tapping, typing, speaking or keying it back.
• Hardware key support: USB and Bluetooth LE MIDI keys, plus full Vail Adapter input and output.
• A quiet background noise floor so Bluetooth earbuds don't sleep through the first character; turn it up and it doubles as band noise.
• A daily practice reminder to keep your streak alive, and a buddy streak: pair with one friend and keep a streak of days you both practised.
• Optional shared leaderboard, off by default, for Rapid Fire, Contest, Pileup Runner and the games.
• Progress tracking: streak, accuracy, fastest copy, most-confused pairs, performance by speed band and a per-character recognition-speed chart.
• iPhone and iPad layouts.

No accounts. No ads. No tracking. Everything stays on your device unless you turn the leaderboard on.

Full user guide: https://anothermorsetrainer.app/guide/
Community and support: https://discord.gg/qgyk3TPUd9

73!
